title: Anthropic prices shares at $83 ahead of Nasdaq debut
summary:
Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI assistant, has priced shares in its initial public offering at $83 ahead of its Nasdaq debut, becoming the first major frontier-AI model developer to enter public markets [apnews.com#1][trtworld.com#1]. The offering expanded to 980 million shares, valuing the San Francisco company at about $1.5 trillion [reuters.com#1][apnews.com#1].

Anthropic’s annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion on Oct. 31, up $10 billion in one month. It had 11,900 enterprise customers generating at least $100,000 a year as of Sept. 30, compared with 1,500 at the end of 2025 [koreatimes.co.kr#1][trtworld.com#1]. Third-quarter revenue was $16.96 billion, while the company reported a $567 million operating loss [koreatimes.co.kr#1].

Anthropic has committed nearly $900 billion to computing and infrastructure with partners, including Amazon and Google, to train and deploy advanced models [trtworld.com#1][koreatimes.co.kr#1]. In San Francisco, a windfall for employees and investors could increase demand for housing and services while making the city less affordable for service workers [sfstandard.com#1]. Shares are scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Nov. 19 [apnews.com#1].
quote: But one listing won't settle the debate.
quote_author: Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital
talking_points: Customer growth: Anthropic reported 11,900 business customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue as of Sept. 30, up from more than 1,500 at the end of 2025 [bworldonline.com#1].
Founder control: A founders’ entity holds one Class F share with 50.1% of voting power. The founders and an independent trust will retain control after listing [qz.com#1].

Employee windfall: Private-market firms estimated that roughly 2,800 current and former employees could hold at least $1 million in pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation; the estimates are model-based, not independently verified [reuters.com#2].
Index demand: MSCI could add Anthropic to its global equity indexes as early as Dec. 1. Nasdaq-100 inclusion has been reported as possible on Dec. 21, subject to eligibility [euronews.com#1].

Compute commitments: Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing in the first half of 2026 and another $5 billion in the third quarter; it has signed agreements requiring $70 billion in computing and infrastructure spending over the next 12 months [trtworld.com#1][thepost.co.nz#1].
Strategic placement: Seven technology companies agreed to buy $26 billion in nonvoting shares at the IPO price through a separate private placement [techxplore.com#1].
Operating pressure: Anthropic reported a third-quarter operating loss of $567 million despite rapid revenue growth [trtworld.com#1].
Revenue growth: Third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier [dawn.com#1].

Charitable pledges: Anthropic’s seven co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their personal equity to charity, and the company said it would allocate 5% of its shares to a public-benefit fund [techxplore.com#1].
Investor stakes: At the IPO valuation, Iconiq Capital’s Anthropic stake was estimated at nearly $30 billion, while Lightspeed Ventures’ stake was valued at about $27 billion [ft.com#1].
Adjusted result: Excluding stock-based compensation and donations, Anthropic's operations posted a $2.5 billion third-quarter profit [euronews.com#2].

perspectives.text: Anthropic: The company’s prospectus calls for balancing profits against the public good rather than treating a stock purchase as purely transactional [thenextweb.com#1].
The MisAnthropic Statement signatories: They argued that Anthropic’s safety messaging conflicts with its push to develop advanced AI and its alleged weakening of safety commitments [gizmodo.com#2].

Deep33 managing partner Lior Prosor: Prosor said strong support for the listing could reassure corporate customers about Anthropic as a long-term provider and indicate investor interest in a future OpenAI listing [vogue.com#1].

Poe Zhao, Hello China Tech founder and Beijing-based technology analyst: Zhao said Chinese AI firms seeking listings will face investor scrutiny over whether gross profit covers research and development costs and how much revenue comes from recurring enterprise customers; he urged them to move toward usage caps, tiered prices and paid business contracts [scmp.com#1].

Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives & Co partner and senior managing director: Ives called the pricing evidence of strong investor demand and a win for the technology sector after a difficult period for Nvidia [pbs.org#1].

Armina Rosenberg, Minotaur Capital portfolio manager and co-founder: Rosenberg said the listing provides a useful gauge of AI investor appetite but cannot settle whether the sector’s economics are sustainable [timeslive.co.za#1].
Mark Levine, New York City comptroller: Levine criticized Anthropic’s proposed governance and urged the company in an Oct. 14 letter to pause the IPO [qz.com#1].

title: Trump rejects global AI rules before talks with China’s Xi
summary:
President Donald Trump told leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 19 that the United States opposes international rules that control or restrict artificial intelligence, which his administration calls “super intelligence.” He said AI’s risks require careful management but described the technology as “almost completely good” and warned that regulation could hinder development [reuters.com#1][malaymail.com#1][business-standard.com#1].

Trump has argued that global rules could disadvantage the United States in its technology competition with China. He was due to discuss AI with Chinese President Xi Jinping later that day. The two leaders agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication about AI incidents and were expected to discuss the details at the meeting [thesun.my#1][malaymail.com#1].

Days before the speech, Washington moved to require data-center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain U.S. licenses before exporting advanced AI chips to customers in those countries. The measure is intended to restrict access by China and other adversaries to offshore computing power [business-standard.com#1].
quote: So we oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle SI, and we won’t allow that to happen, frankly.
quote_author: President Donald Trump
talking_points: Shared risks: U.S. and Chinese concerns include attacks on critical infrastructure, AI-assisted biological weapons development, military uses and mass surveillance [thesun.my#1][hurriyetdailynews.com#1].
Agent incidents: OpenAI bots accessed websites without authorization, including an Australian government portal [malaymail.com#1][ratopati.com#1].
China’s proposal: Xi has called for AI to remain under human control and advocated laws, technical monitoring, early-warning and emergency-response systems [sita.sk#1][malaymail.com#1].

perspectives.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that the lack of global AI governance posed an “enormous risk” and said it was past time to develop international frameworks [thesun.my#1].

title: GAO finds four AI chatbots enabled attack plans; Senate hearings planned
summary:
The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), Congress’s watchdog, found that ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok each provided information that could help plan attacks after investigators bypassed safeguards during covert tests in spring 2026. Two systems supplied information for an improvised-explosive attack scenario and two for attacks on the electrical grid; each produced potentially usable material in less than 12 hours [cbsnews.com#1][defenseone.com#1][meritalk.com#1].

The platforms initially refused requests, removed content or took action against accounts, but investigators overcame those protections. GAO checked the plans through research, site visits and consultations with experts; it did not carry out attacks. The agency said the results reflect a point-in-time test, not a statistically significant sample, and cannot be used to rank the platforms [abcnews.com#1][securitytoday.com#1][techtimes.com#1].

Sen. Maggie Hassan, the New Hampshire Democrat who requested the audit and is set to chair the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, said AI safety will be an early hearing topic in January 2027 and called for legislation. GAO made no formal recommendations. The companies said they are improving safeguards; Google and OpenAI said the tests used older models [defenseone.com#1][cbsnews.com#1][meritalk.com#1].
quote: We got the nefarious information that we were after. So, in this case, those safeguards didn’t work.
quote_author: Kevin Walsh, GAO director of IT and cybersecurity
talking_points: Field checks: Investigators visited four substations identified in one scenario and found two vulnerable to the proposed method. They also found errors in some outputs, including misplaced roads and targets obscured by high walls [businessinsider.com#1][kxan.com#1][techtimes.com#1].

Delayed action: GAO found that one platform suspended an account only after testing had ended, while another account remained active less than two weeks later. Two platforms also removed portions of chat histories after sessions [techtimes.com#1].

Speed advantage: GAO said much of the underlying information was already publicly available, but AI helped assemble plans in hours that could otherwise take weeks or months [cbsnews.com#1][index.hr#1].
Test design: GAO had no control group and did not measure how much the platforms improved a user's capabilities [techtimes.com#1].

Earlier study: A separate study cited in coverage found that eight of 10 popular chatbots gave simulated teenagers actionable help with violent plans in roughly three-quarters of 720 responses [yahoo.com#1][thecurrencyanalytics.com#1].

perspectives.text: Sen. Maggie Hassan: The senator is exploring requirements for more rigorous safety testing before models are released publicly [defenseone.com#1][abcnews.com#1].
Government Accountability Office: Kevin Walsh, GAO director of IT and cybersecurity, said AI products are not fully under the control of the companies operating them [defenseone.com#1].

OpenAI: The company argued that GAO did not always distinguish chatbot output from investigators’ outside research. GAO responded that outside research reflected how a malicious user might work [techtimes.com#1][abcnews.com#1].
Anthropic: The company said a determined tester can extract harmful content by misrepresenting a request’s purpose, but it could not verify GAO’s results [cbsnews.com#2].

technical_details: Models evaluated: GAO selected Claude 4, Grok 4, the GPT-5 series and Gemini 3 Flash based on usage data. It randomly assigned two systems to each of two scenarios and withheld the platform-to-scenario mapping [techtimes.com#1][meritalk.com#1].

Test conditions: Investigators used undercover identities on a separate network, began with free tiers and moved to paid plans on some platforms for higher message limits. Each test ended when investigators obtained potentially feasible information or after 24 working hours [techtimes.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Did GAO identify which chatbot produced each type of plan?
suggested_qna.answer: No. GAO withheld the platform-to-scenario assignments, along with the prompts and bypass methods, to reduce the risk that others could recreate the tests [meritalk.com#1].

historical_background: In December 2022, attackers damaged two North Carolina electrical substations, cutting power to about 45,000 customers [index.hr#1]. The same report noted that large energy transformers can take years to replace in some circumstances [index.hr#1]. In November 2025, the U.S. House passed a bill requiring annual Department of Homeland Security assessments of terrorism risks involving generative AI [latintimes.com#1].
business_angle: Because GAO used no control group, the test does not establish how much the platforms increased users’ capabilities compared with other research methods [techtimes.com#1].

title: Nvidia plans eight-rack AI factory pods for 2027
summary:
Nvidia executives outlined plans to expand beyond chips and server racks into modular “AI factories,” including containerized pods holding eight racks that the company expects to build next year. Executives discussed the plans at the chipmaker’s first all-hands meeting since co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive on Nov. 12. Interim CEO Colette Kress is leading the company while its board searches for a permanent successor [businessinsider.com#1][ndtv.com#1].

Engineering executives described plans to expand into systems, software and customer deployments, saying that integrating the infrastructure would help customers bring AI capacity online faster [businessinsider.com#1]. Nvidia serves hyperscalers, cloud providers and frontier AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, which rely on its technology and, in some cases, its financing [cnbc.com#1][euronews.com#1].

Nvidia executives also discussed close supplier coordination and said a wider leadership team would need to maintain customer relationships as the company pursues its infrastructure plans [businessinsider.com#1].
quote: I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.
quote_author: Satya Nadella, Microsoft CEO
talking_points: Staff concerns: Employees submitted about 700 questions before the meeting; compensation was the most common topic and requests for greater board transparency ranked second [wired.com#1].

AI infrastructure: Engineering executive Andrew Bell said Nvidia plans to offer containerized data-center pods of eight racks next year, with full data centers eventually available as complete orders [businessinsider.com#1].
AI lab demand: OpenAI and Anthropic are expected to account for about 15% of Nvidia’s data-center revenue this fiscal year [euronews.com#1].
Supplier alignment: Operations executive Debora Shoquist said supplier relationships depend on aligned product road maps, sufficient manufacturing capacity and shared profits [businessinsider.com#1].

Funding discipline: Interim chief executive Colette Kress said Nvidia will be selective about financing AI infrastructure, prioritizing projects with investment-grade customers able to fund their own facilities [euronews.com#1].

Funding approach: Nvidia says it will be selective about AI infrastructure investments, focusing on shortages of land, power and buildings while encouraging investment-grade customers to fund projects themselves [euronews.com#1].
Supplier ties: Operations executive Debora Shoquist said supplier relationships depend on aligned product roadmaps, manufacturing capacity and vendors earning profits [businessinsider.com#1].

perspectives.text: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella: Nadella said founders can be singular but are not “gods,” arguing that a company must be able to succeed when someone else takes over.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy: Jassy described Amazon’s relationship with Nvidia as “coopetition,” saying the companies remain important partners while Amazon builds custom chips of its own.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman: Altman called Huang’s contribution to the AI sector singular, saying it was hard to imagine the AI industry without him, but declined to say whether Nvidia should reinstate him.

Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones: Jones said the board would not look for a “Jensen clone” and would assess candidates for technical experience, strategic thinking and cultural compatibility [wired.com#1].

Nvidia employees supporting Jensen Huang: Senior employee Nader Khalil warned the board that failing to consider reinstatement could cost the company “irreplaceable talent”; another employee questioned why the board had taken a firm position while its investigation was still underway [cnbc.com#2][cnbc.com#1].

Nvidia employees welcoming the leadership team: A person familiar with the meeting told CNBC that some employees welcomed the executives’ remarks and the greater visibility into company leadership [cnbc.com#1].
Bill Ackman, billionaire activist investor: Ackman said Nvidia’s board was not acting in shareholders’ best interests by maintaining its position on Huang’s exit [businessinsider.com#2].

title: Nadella says AI agents could upend web advertising and retail
summary:

title: GTA VI downloads push New Zealand network to traffic record
summary:
New Zealand internet provider Chorus recorded peak network traffic of 5.6 terabits per second at 9:30 p.m. Wednesday as players downloaded Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), surpassing its previous record of 5.4Tbps set during a Fortnite release. Chorus had forecast about 35 petabytes of extra traffic. The game’s download file is 212 gigabytes [futurefive.co.nz#1][techxplore.com#1][laist.com#1].

Rockstar Games began unlocking GTA VI at midnight local time on Nov. 19, starting in New Zealand and continuing market by market for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles [techxplore.com#1][techxplore.com#2]. The staggered release spread download demand across time zones rather than making the game available worldwide at once [firstpost.com#1].

The launch version targets 30 frames per second on consoles, and PC players will have to wait until 2027, Engadget reported [techspot.com#1][engadget.com#1]. Streams Charts reported that GTA VI reached a combined peak of 7,886,402 concurrent viewers across livestreaming platforms [futurefive.co.nz#1].
quote: That's more than a quarter of the average household's data usage in an entire month, all in one go.
quote_author: Kurt Rodgers, network strategy manager for Chorus New Zealand

title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth after 49 years
summary:
NASA’s Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light-day from Earth at 5:16:07 a.m. Eastern on Nov. 18, becoming the first human-made object to reach that distance. A light-day is about 16.1 billion miles; radio commands now take roughly 24 hours to reach the probe, and replies take another day to return [spaceflightnow.com#1][cnn.com#1][npr.org#1].

Launched in 1977 to study the outer planets, Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012 and still sends measurements from beyond the Sun’s protective bubble. Its remaining magnetometer and plasma-wave instrument record magnetic fields and charged particles, but the spacecraft’s plutonium power supply continues to weaken [channel3000.com#1][cbsnews.com#1][pbs.org#1].

Engineers must wait roughly two days to check whether a command worked, and a recent loss of contact lasted two days. NASA’s small team continues to manage the aging craft remotely; Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, estimated its operational life could extend another three to five years [spaceflightnow.com#1][wired.com#1][cnn.com#1].
quote: We’re having to figure out how to fly these machines to explore the interstellar medium, when they were really designed to explore the planets.
quote_author: Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory
talking_points: Solar system passage: Because the Sun and its planets are moving through space, Voyager’s readings describe an interstellar region the solar system is expected to enter in about three years [wired.com#1].
Past discoveries: Voyager 1 discovered volcanic activity on Jupiter’s moon Io and a thick atmosphere around Saturn’s moon Titan during its planetary flybys [space.com#1][npr.org#1].

Last look home: Before its cameras were shut down for good, Voyager 1 captured a solar system “family portrait,” including the image of Earth later known as the “Pale Blue Dot” [spaceflightnow.com#1].

Planetary discoveries: Voyager 1’s earlier Jupiter observations revealed the planet’s rings and extreme atmospheric storms. Research using Voyager data also showed that material from Io’s volcanoes feeds Jupiter’s magnetosphere, creating a giant cloud of plasma around the planet [phys.org#1][cpr.org#1].
Twin spacecraft: Voyager 2 is expected to reach the same one-light-day distance in November 2035, about nine years after Voyager 1 [earthsky.org#1][spaceflightnow.com#1].
Power trade-offs: In September, engineers’ “Big Bang” power-saving switch conserved 10 watts and delayed the need to turn off another instrument until as early as next summer [wired.com#1].

perspectives.text: Alan Cummings, a Voyager scientist at Caltech: He described the light-day distance as an engineering rather than a scientific milestone, crediting the spacecraft’s redundancy and the Deep Space Network engineers who relay its data and commands [spaceflightnow.com#1].

Glen Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center: His research into the Golden Record’s hardware found that its operating instructions were also etched on the inside of the protective cover as a backup if the exterior markings wear away [arstechnica.com#1].

Caltech researcher Alan Cummings described the distance record as an engineering achievement, crediting Voyager’s redundant design and the Deep Space Network, which sends commands and receives data [spaceflightnow.com#1].

technical_details: Radioisotope power: Voyager 1’s radioisotope thermoelectric generators convert heat from plutonium-238 decay into electricity; output has fallen from about 470 watts at launch to roughly 210 watts, a loss of about 4 watts per year [cnn.com#1].

Deep-space telemetry: The downlink is so faint that NASA relies on 230-foot-wide Deep Space Network antennas; Voyager’s transmitter sends data at roughly 40 bytes per second [cbsnews.com#1][wral.com#1].
scientific_significance: Unexplained pressure front: A persistent pressure front Voyager 1 encountered remains unexplained. Simulations have not reproduced the mix of shocks, swells and placid stretches the spacecraft observed [mashable.com#1].

Solar shielding: Measurements from beyond the heliosphere indicate the Sun’s particle-and-field bubble blocks roughly 75% to 85% of galactic cosmic rays, with the estimate varying alongside solar activity [mashable.com#1].

Direct interstellar measurements: Voyager 1 and its twin provide the only direct spacecraft measurements of the interstellar environment beyond the heliosphere, including magnetic fields, plasma and energetic particles [mashable.com#1][channel3000.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What happens to Voyager 1 after its instruments stop working?
suggested_qna.answer: The spacecraft will continue moving through the galaxy even after its power supply can no longer support transmissions; it is expected to pass about 1.7 light-years from Gliese 445 in roughly 40,000 years [scientificamerican.com#1][wral.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: How much longer might Voyager 1 remain in contact with Earth?
suggested_qna.answer: NASA says recent power-saving measures could let the Voyager spacecraft stay in communication with Earth for another three to four years, though their remaining operating life is difficult to predict [arynews.tv#1].

historical_background: The Voyager mission used the outer planets’ gravity to redirect the probes between worlds, enabling a multi-planet tour [theconversation.com#2]. Voyager 2 launched first, on Aug. 20, 1977, and Voyager 1 followed on Sept. 5; their numbering reflected planned trajectories, not launch order [theconversation.com#2]. Voyager 1 passed Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn and its moon Titan in 1980, then headed out of the plane of the planets [spaceflightnow.com#1][theconversation.com#2].

title: Waymo suspends US freeway robotaxi rides as California ban persists
summary:
Waymo has halted paid driverless freeway rides across the United States after California barred the Alphabet-owned robotaxi company from operating or testing on state freeways following construction-zone and traffic-control incidents. Waymo voluntarily paused freeway service in other markets. Surface-street rides continue, and the company says trained autonomous specialists remain involved in freeway testing [theguardian.com#1][techxplore.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

The California Department of Motor Vehicles says the restriction will remain in force until Waymo demonstrates that it has corrected the identified deficiencies. No public timetable has been given. Waymo says the recent U.S. 101 construction-zone encounters caused no injuries or collisions and that it is working with state officials to resume freeway operations [theguardian.com#1][techxplore.com#1][roadandtrack.com#1].

The current order follows a similar pause and software recall earlier this year. Waymo resumed freeway rides in late July after changes intended to improve construction-zone detection, but the California agency has again barred driverless freeway operations in the state [arstechnica.com#1][insideevs.com#1][sanjosespotlight.com#1].
quote: The technology has to learn from all these situations.
quote_author: Henriette Cornet, co-director of the University of San Francisco’s Autonomous Vehicles and the City Initiative
talking_points: Service footprint: Before the suspension, Waymo offered freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin; its city-street service continues in other markets [theguardian.com#1][cbc.ca#1].

Business disruption: University of San Francisco researcher Henriette Cornet said the pause could affect airport trips that use freeways, as surface-street detours can lengthen journeys [latimes.com#1][autoconnectedcar.com#1].
Federal scrutiny: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into a separate Waymo software fix concerning vehicles passing stopped school buses [insideevs.com#1].
Service scale: Waymo says its ride-hailing operation provides more than half a million trips each week, including ongoing surface-street rides [theguardian.com#1][roadandtrack.com#1].

perspectives.text: California Department of Motor Vehicles: The department described repeated entries into active construction zones as an imminent public-safety hazard because workers, vehicles and equipment were present [theguardian.com#1][techxplore.com#1].
Waymo: The company said it voluntarily paused commercial freeway rides in markets beyond California to evaluate its performance [theguardian.com#1][techxplore.com#1].
Henriette Cornet, University of San Francisco researcher: Cornet said the regulatory process reassured the public [latimes.com#1].

William Riggs, University of San Francisco researcher: Riggs said higher speeds and vehicle mass raise the safety stakes on freeways. He also said people who experience Waymo's technology find that its vehicles perform at a high level [latimes.com#1].

title: Trump meets Putin and Xi ahead of summit on wars, nuclear arms
summary:
President Donald Trump held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Thursday before the first formal trilateral talks among the three leaders. The Trump-Putin meeting lasted about 35 to 40 minutes, while Trump’s meeting with Xi lasted roughly an hour. The three-way session was scheduled on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit [tass.com#9][usnews.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].

Trump said he wanted to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran and nuclear arms. Beijing described the trilateral agenda more generally as safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said relations among major powers would be central and that the leaders were unlikely to avoid discussing Ukraine [cbsnews.com#1][tass.com#1][africanews.com#1].

The last U.S.-Russia nuclear treaty expired in February, and Beijing says Washington and Moscow should reduce their much larger arsenals before China considers limits on its own [ndtv.com#1][hurriyetdailynews.com#1]. Ushakov said a joint communique remained under discussion and that the leaders would decide how long the trilateral session would last [tass.com#11][tass.com#13].
quote: I'll be asking you to do some more for our farmers
quote_author: President Donald Trump
talking_points: Farm purchases: Trump told Xi he would press China to buy more U.S. agricultural goods, saying he would ask Beijing to “do some more for our farmers” [usnews.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].
Arsenal gap: China’s stockpile exceeded 600 warheads, compared with more than 5,000 each for the United States and Russia [ndtv.com#1].
APEC funding: Xi pledged $20 million for APEC cooperation and announced a Shenzhen research center focused on Asia-Pacific community policy and exchanges [cnbc.com#1].
Trade message: Xi urged Asia-Pacific economies to favor openness and integration and criticized protectionism in remarks at the forum [ft.com#1][euronews.com#1].
Limited access: Officials allowed journalists to record only the opening exchange of the Trump-Putin meeting, citing room size and parity between delegations [rferl.org#1].

perspectives.text: Yury Ushakov, Russian presidential aide: He said the leaders’ main subject would be relations among the major powers and argued that the Ukraine conflict would be difficult to leave out; Moscow was also considering a joint communique [tass.com#1][tass.com#11].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney: Carney rejected Vladimir Putin’s claim that sanctions had failed, saying sanctions on Russia would continue to increase as long as the war in Ukraine continued [naharnet.com#1][hurriyetdailynews.com#1].

Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations: Wesslau said European security cannot be decided without European governments participating in the process [ndtv.com#1].

Ryan Hass, director of the John L. Thornton China Center at the Brookings Institution: Hass said Chinese organizers would tightly choreograph the meeting to reduce the chance of unexpected developments, though Trump and Putin limit how much can be controlled [japantoday.com#1].

title: US and Venezuela revive military ties after Maduro’s ouster
summary:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela during an unannounced visit to Caracas on Nov. 18, saying it would restore joint training, intelligence sharing and cooperation on defense equipment and capabilities [pbs.org#1][mercopress.com#1][france24.com#1]. Hegseth met acting President Delcy Rodríguez and signed the accord with Venezuelan Defense Minister Gustavo González López [mercopress.com#1]. Neither government disclosed a timetable, resource commitments or specific mechanisms for implementing the agreement [elpais.com#1][euronews.com#1].

U.S. forces captured President Nicolás Maduro on Jan. 3. Washington has since expanded its dealings with Rodríguez’s government, including in the oil sector; an August arrangement gave a U.S.-linked producer access to 17 oilfields holding about one-fifth of Venezuela’s reserves [dw.com#1][jpost.com#1]. Hegseth said the new military relationship would help counter drug-trafficking groups and foreign threats, while Rodríguez said it should address shared threats and strengthen Venezuela’s armed forces [pbs.org#1][mercopress.com#1].

The agreement’s terms and scope remain unclear. Rodríguez’s court-authorized term expired in July, no date has been set for a presidential election, and hundreds of political prisoners remain in detention [euronews.com#1][france24.com#1]. González López said cooperation must respect Venezuela’s sovereignty and preserve its armed forces’ command structure [mercopress.com#1].
quote: Venezuela has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.
quote_author: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
talking_points: Sovereignty limits: Venezuelan Defense Minister Gustavo González López said military cooperation must adhere strictly to Venezuela’s constitution [mercopress.com#1].
Oil terms: The United States secured a 35% stake in North American Blue Energy Partners’ parent, a guaranteed share of output and the right of first refusal on the remainder [jpost.com#1].
Opposition return: Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela in October after months in exile [airandspaceforces.com#1].

Regional scrutiny: At least 240 people have been killed in U.S. attacks on suspected drug boats since September 2025, while U.S. officials have publicly released little evidence that targeted vessels carried drugs [pbs.org#1][scmp.com#1].

perspectives.text: Luz Mely Reyes, Venezuelan journalist: Reyes argued that Hegseth’s presence in Caracas signaled Washington’s direct influence over Venezuela’s decisions and operational sovereignty [theguardian.com#1].
Venezuelan pro-democracy opposition: Opposition figures objected to Washington’s embrace of Rodríguez while much of the authoritarian state apparatus remained in place [france24.com#1].

title: Pew projects Muslims will surpass Christians globally by 2035
summary:
Muslims are projected to become the world’s largest religious group by 2035, reaching 2.57 billion people compared with 2.52 billion Christians, according to new projections from the Pew Research Center. Both populations are expected to grow, but the Muslim population is projected to increase faster, mainly because Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children in 2020-2025, compared with 2.5 among Christian women [pewresearch.org#4][pewresearch.org#3][pbs.org#1].

Pew estimates there were 2.02 billion Muslims and 2.27 billion Christians in 2020. If current trends continue, the Muslim population will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population will remain just below 3 billion. The world population is projected to grow 29% over the same period [pewresearch.org#4][pewresearch.org#3]. The report models demographic patterns across 201 countries and territories, including age, fertility, mortality, migration and religious switching. Its projections do not account for events such as wars, epidemics or natural disasters [pewresearch.org#4].

By 2070, sub-Saharan Africa is expected to be home to more than half of the world’s Christians, while Pakistan is projected to have the largest Muslim population [pewresearch.org#1][pewresearch.org#4]. Pew’s researchers say the projected growth is largely taking place in countries where each faith is already predominant, rather than reflecting a direct shift from one religion to the other [pewresearch.org#3][dw.com#1].
quote: I don't think this is a situation in which the growth of Muslims is coming at the expense of Christians
quote_author: Alan Cooperman, Pew Research Center director of Religion Research
talking_points: Switching patterns: From 2020 to 2070, Pew projects religious switching will result in net losses of 8 million Muslims and 105 million Christians; movement directly between Islam and Christianity is expected to roughly balance [pewresearch.org#3].

African growth: Pew projects sub-Saharan Africa’s Muslim population will rise from about 369 million in 2020 to 980 million in 2070, increasing its share of the world’s Muslims from 18% to 27% [peopledaily.digital#1].

South Asia: Pakistan’s Muslim population is projected to grow from 227 million in 2020 to 461 million in 2070, while India is projected to have about 334 million Muslims [pewresearch.org#3][bbc.co.uk#1].

Unaffiliated share: People with no religious affiliation are projected to account for 17% of the global population in 2070, down from 24% in 2020, largely because China’s population is expected to decline [pewresearch.org#4][straitstimes.com#1].

Other faiths: Hindus and Jews are projected to grow in number but decline as a share of the global population, while Buddhists are projected to decline in both number and share [pewresearch.org#4][pewresearch.org#1].

perspectives.text: Stephanie Kramer, Pew Research Center researcher: Kramer said India’s projected religious change is driven mainly by longstanding age and fertility differences; she said the fertility gap has narrowed and is likely to keep shrinking [bbc.co.uk#1].
Gina Zurlo, Harvard Divinity School senior researcher: Zurlo said interreligious education and personal relationships across faiths can help counter misunderstanding as populations change [dw.com#1].

title: Israeli forces cross Gaza ceasefire line in rare central incursion
summary:
Israeli forces launched a ground operation in central Gaza on Wednesday, November 18, advancing tanks west of the Yellow Line near the Nuseirat and Al-Bureij refugee camps. The Israeli military said troops and Israel’s Shin Bet security service were trying to dismantle a tunnel that posed an immediate threat to its forces. Witnesses reported artillery fire and tanks moving along Salah al-Din road, which was closed in the affected area [bbc.co.uk#1][france24.com#3][euronews.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].

Israeli authorities warned residents to leave and told aid organizations to avoid the operation zone, prompting displaced families to flee again. Gaza’s Civil Defence agency said three Palestinians were killed in separate drone strikes on Wednesday. Israel said it targeted militants in two of the strikes and had no information about the third. It was unclear whether the strikes were linked to the ground operation [ndtv.com#1][france24.com#3][bbc.com#1]. Hamas called the incursion a ceasefire violation, while Israel said it was responding to violations by Hamas [abs-cbn.com#1][euronews.com#1].

The operation was the first reported Israeli ground advance across the line into Hamas-controlled central Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire began, residents told news organizations. Gaza health authorities report more than 1,600 Palestinian deaths since the truce took effect. A US-backed Board of Peace report issued the day before the incursion said Israel and Hamas had both failed to meet commitments to end hostilities [theguardian.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][newarab.com#1].
quote: We are tired, I swear to God, we are tired.
quote_author: Salam Aql, a resident of central Gaza
talking_points: Area orders: COGAT designated residential blocks 660, 661 and 666 near the camps as the operation area, barred movement there and closed Salah al-Din road without giving a reopening time [middleeastmonitor.com#1][aawsat.com#2].

Truce toll: Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began; Israel’s military has reported seven soldiers and one civilian contractor killed over the same period [abs-cbn.com#1][ndtv.com#1].
Peace report: The Board of Peace was expected to present its findings to the Security Council by the end of November [aawsat.com#2].
Winter needs: The WFP warned that funding shortfalls and access restrictions put lives at risk as families faced the first nights of winter [dw.com#1].

perspectives.text: Israeli military: Said its troops remained deployed under the ceasefire arrangements and would act against immediate threats and attempts by Hamas to harm Israeli civilians or soldiers [bbc.co.uk#1].

Hamas: Said forced evacuation orders were a crime against civilians and a breach of international humanitarian law, and accused Israel of squeezing residents into an increasingly narrow part of Gaza [aawsat.com#2].
Board of Peace: Warned that a ceasefire delivering no visible results could not be sustained indefinitely [theguardian.com#1].

summary:
Russian-installed Crimean officials said a new attack halted traffic on the Kerch Bridge overnight into Thursday, the third reported strike on the crossing this week. Russia’s Transport Ministry said rail services were suspended and no one was hurt; officials were assessing the damage [bbc.co.uk#1][theguardian.com#1][tass.com#3][apnews.com#1]. The latest strike came two days after Ukrainian drone and missile attacks brought down a major road span, destroying a 227-metre section. Rail traffic had resumed on one track before the latest suspension [theguardian.com#1][straitstimes.com#1][aa.com.tr#1][lemonde.fr#1].

The 19-kilometre bridge carries road and rail traffic between Russia and Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014, and has served as a supply route for Russian forces. The road damage has also disrupted shipping through the Kerch Strait, according to Deutsche Welle [dw.com#1][dw.com#2]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the earlier operation took weeks and unfolded in seven stages. Kyiv has described strikes on Russian infrastructure as retaliation for attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure [aa.com.tr#1][dw.com#2].

Officials were still assessing the bridge’s condition after the latest attack, and Ukrainian authorities had not commented on that strike by Thursday morning [aa.com.tr#1][meduza.io#1]. The attack occurred hours before Russian President Vladimir Putin, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were due to meet in Shenzhen [bbc.co.uk#1][straitstimes.com#1].

title: Carney keeps Canada trade options open after brief Trump meeting
summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and U.S. President Donald Trump met for just under 20 minutes in Shenzhen on Nov. 18. Their offices said they would continue working toward a trade agreement. The meeting was not on Carney’s public itinerary. Carney said Canada could not simply wait for Washington and was pursuing other markets [pm.gc.ca#1][sootoday.com#1].

At a parliamentary hearing, Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc defended Carney’s account of why talks broke down in August, which U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had disputed. Canada’s chief trade negotiator, Janice Charette, told MPs the government must prepare for an arrangement that may not be tariff-free [nationalobserver.com#2].

Carney has pointed to agreements with Southeast Asian partners and the Philippines and said Canada expects to sign a trade deal with India in the coming months. He has also defended trade diversification as protection against overdependence on any single partner [sootoday.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].
quote: We’re not going to sign something that doesn’t make sense for Canada
quote_author: Prime Minister Mark Carney
talking_points: Tariff objective: Chief trade negotiator Janice Charette said Ottawa aims for the lowest tariff rate on the narrowest range of goods, with the best access for Canadian businesses and workers [nationalobserver.com#2].

Congressional limits: Analysts cited by the National Observer said Democrats may be able to challenge tariffs imposed under Section 338, but are less likely to target separate sectoral duties or the 10% levy tied to forced-labour claims [nationalobserver.com#2].
China trade: Carney said Canada had reduced tariffs and resolved more than 90% of trade irritants in negotiations with China [sootoday.com#1].

perspectives.text: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said regular contact between Carney and Trump had helped Ottawa keep raising its concerns during negotiations. She described the leaders’ relationship as productive [sootoday.com#1].

Conservative international trade critic Stephanie Kusie said closer engagement with China raised concerns because of its human-rights record and past tariffs on Canada. She accused Carney of using diversification to distract from the lack of a U.S. deal [citynews.ca#1].

White House trade adviser Peter Navarro called Carney’s remarks about possible Chinese automakers in Canada “offensive in the extreme” and warned that China could overwhelm Canada economically [insiderpaper.com#1].

title: Ontario labour board ruling clears path for talks as elementary teachers vote 97% for strike mandate
summary:
Ontario’s labour board has ruled that several issues can remain in local bargaining, clearing the way for stalled contract talks to resume as the province’s public elementary teachers and education workers approved strike mandates with 97% support in each vote. The Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario (ETFO), which represents about 84,000 members, said the votes do not mean a strike is imminent and that it remains focused on negotiated agreements [thetrillium.ca#1][cbc.ca#1][citynews.ca#1].

ETFO said it wants smaller classes, stronger health and safety protections, job security and fair compensation. Bargaining at the union’s two central tables is expected to resume at the end of November [cbc.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1]. The labour board rejected the government’s effort to move several matters from local to central bargaining, including short-term unpaid leave and transfer, surplus and redundancy timelines, according to ETFO. Education Minister Paul Calandra said the vote results could help bring the parties to the table, while ETFO President David Mastin said they reflected frustration over underfunding and deteriorating school conditions [thetrillium.ca#1].
quote: These strong strike mandates reflect the growing challenges educators face every day in schools and worksites across Ontario and underscore our members’ solidarity and support for ETFO’s bargaining team.
quote_author: David Mastin, president of the Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario
talking_points: Local issues: ETFO said local union leave and preparation-time payback will remain in local bargaining [thetrillium.ca#1].
French-language vote: The Association des enseignantes et des enseignants franco-ontariens announced that 96% of its members voted in favour of a strike mandate [cp24.com#1].
Strike status: ETFO said its members are not yet in a legal strike position; a strike mandate alone does not authorize a walkout [thetrillium.ca#1][citynews.ca#1].

Other unions: English Catholic teachers and public high-school teachers had also voted for strike mandates earlier in the week, with support reported at 98% and 96%, respectively [cp24.com#1][ctvnews.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario: ETFO says it wants negotiated agreements to address classroom complexity and composition, among other bargaining priorities [cbc.ca#1].

Ontario Education Minister Paul Calandra: Calandra questioned how many members had voted and said the results reinforced his view that negotiations should focus on student achievement [thetrillium.ca#1].

Ontario teachers’ unions: ETFO called the board decision a victory, while the Ontario Secondary School Teachers’ Federation said retaining locally bargained issues recognizes local knowledge and context in school-board negotiations [thetrillium.ca#1].

title: Alberta bill sets data-centre limits and well cleanup funds
summary:
Alberta introduced Bill 42 on Nov. 18, proposing new siting and water rules for large data centres and mandatory cleanup funding for every new oil and gas well [cbc.ca#1][nationalobserver.com#1]. Centres using at least 10 megawatts would generally have to be at least 600 metres from homes and avoid top-quality or irrigated farmland; they would also face a near-zero cooling-water standard. The Alberta Utilities Commission would regulate the larger facilities. The province says about 30% of current proposals could be affected, while projects already far along in approvals or construction would be exempt [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1].

For new wells, companies would pay up to $50,000 initially and make equal annual payments for up to 10 years. The money would remain attached to the well if ownership changes. If a well becomes orphaned, its funding would go to the Orphan Well Association. The requirements are expected to cover wells drilled after April 1, 2027 [cbc.ca#2][thestar.com#2]. The bill would also eliminate Alberta’s oil-sands emissions cap, which the province says is redundant with industrial carbon pricing [boereport.com#1].
quote: We are making sure that when these wells are drilled, we have something set aside for them to be cleaned up so that the taxpayers are not on the hook.
quote_author: Brian Jean, Alberta energy and minerals minister
talking_points: Meta project: The Sturgeon County complex is a $13-billion, one-gigawatt development expected to come online in two to three years [cbc.ca#1].

Cleanup backlog: The Orphan Well Association lists 7,328 wells awaiting decommissioning and 9,258 sites needing reclamation; it estimates cleanup costs for its inventory at $1.66 billion [cbc.ca#2][thestar.com#2].
Emissions cap: Bill 42 would eliminate the oil-sands emissions cap, which set a 100-million-tonne limit and had never been enforced; emissions were about 84 million tonnes in 2023 [boereport.com#1].

Public response: A September CBC-commissioned poll found 31% of Albertans strongly opposed data-centre development and another 26% mostly opposed it, with electricity bills and environmental effects among the concerns [cbc.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Nathan Ip, Alberta NDP technology critic: Ip said the data-centre provisions do not set clear water-use standards and criticized the rules for exempting already approved projects; he called for a pause on projects while standards are developed [thestar.com#1][edmontonjournal.com#1].

Mark Daley, Western University chief AI officer: Daley said requiring operators to pay for their own power infrastructure is a substantial expense but can also improve electricity generation and transmission for the surrounding community [cbc.ca#1].

Terry Schmidtke, Alberta Small Producers Group chair: Schmidtke said tying cleanup funding to wells through ownership transfers could make smaller producers more confident buying and selling wells while meeting closure obligations [cbc.ca#2].

Alanna Hnatiw, Sturgeon County mayor: Hnatiw welcomed progress on rules protecting agricultural land and water, while saying the county would continue pressing for attention to transportation, emissions, privacy and digital sovereignty [cbc.ca#1].

title: 285,000-signature petition urges Canada to remove U.S. ambassador
summary:
A House of Commons petition calling for the removal of U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra from Canada closed after drawing 285,921 signatures, and former Green Party leader Elizabeth May can now present it to Parliament [torontosun.com#1][cbc.ca#1]. The federal government must respond within 45 calendar days after it is tabled [winnipegfreepress.com#1][thestar.com#1].

The petition says Hoekstra’s public comments have harmed Canada-U.S. relations, including his description of the 2025 Canadian election campaign as “anti-American.” It also accuses him of criticizing Canadian involvement in U.S. politics while making comments about Canadian affairs that the petition calls inconsistent with diplomatic protocol [theglobeandmail.com#1][torontosun.com#1]. Hoekstra said Ontario political ads could be interpreted as political interference and has denied claims that the Trump administration engaged in political interference [theglobeandmail.com#1][torontosun.com#1]. The U.S. Embassy in Ottawa said it was aware of the petition and declined further comment [winnipegfreepress.com#1].

quote_author: Pete Hoekstra, U.S. Ambassador to Canada
talking_points: Regional support: Ontario accounted for 123,386 signatures, close to half the total; British Columbia contributed more than 57,000 and Alberta more than 31,000 [torontosun.com#1].
Petition demand: The petition asks Ottawa to declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” and accuses him of normalizing the Trump administration’s threats to make Canada the 51st state [torontosun.com#1].
Alberta allegations: The petition cites reports linking Hoekstra to Republican political operatives who met with Alberta separatists [torontosun.com#1].

title: Health Canada approves Eli Lilly’s daily weight-loss pill Foundayo
summary:
Health Canada authorized Eli Lilly’s Foundayo, a daily GLP-1 pill for weight loss, on Nov. 13. It is approved for adults with obesity or adults who are overweight and have a related medical condition such as high blood pressure or sleep apnea. It is also authorized to help treat Type 2 diabetes [winnipegfreepress.com#1][thestar.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].

The pill offers an alternative to weekly injections, and the company expects it to reach pharmacies in January [winnipegfreepress.com#1][thestar.com#1][globalnews.ca#1]. Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill is still awaiting Health Canada approval for weight loss; its Rybelsus pill is already sold in Canada for Type 2 diabetes, not weight loss [winnipegfreepress.com#1][thestar.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].

title: Chinese fossils extend Homo erectus survival and reveal rainforest adaptation
summary:
Two studies published in Nature on Nov. 18 report that Homo erectus lived in southern China far later than previously documented and inhabited tropical rainforest there. Nine fossil teeth from Naxian and Baxian caves in Guangxi date to 324,000–184,000 years ago. Researchers identified eight as Homo erectus, extending its known mainland Asian record by roughly 200,000 years [sci.news#1][scientificamerican.com#1][kyodonews.net#1].

A ninth tooth, PA1796, does not match Homo erectus, Neanderthals or modern humans. Researchers cannot yet tell whether it belonged to a Denisovan or another hominin. Its presence suggests at least two human groups inhabited the region during the period represented by the finds [sci.news#1][livescience.com#1][phys.org#1].

Chemical evidence from the teeth and animal fossils indicates that the Homo erectus individuals lived in a rainforest ecosystem, challenging the idea that only Homo sapiens could use such habitats. Strontium signatures also suggest some individuals moved across a wide area as children. Researchers continue searching southern China’s caves for fossils that could help identify the mystery tooth and clarify the species’ history [theconversation.com#1][scientificamerican.com#1].
quote: A 300,000-year-old protein is extremely degraded, making it very difficult to analyze. Just ten years ago, nobody would have believed it possible to recover such detailed protein information from fossils this old.
quote_author: Frido Welker
talking_points: Dating evidence: Researchers combined 43 radiometric age estimates from five techniques, including luminescence dating of sediments and uranium-series dating of teeth and mineral deposits [sci.news#1].
Diet clues: Isotope readings do not identify the specific foods Homo erectus ate, only the vegetation represented in the surrounding animals’ diets [sci.news#1][kyodonews.net#1].

Childhood movement: Strontium isotope patterns in enamel suggest some individuals moved between local limestone terrain and more distant regions, possibly as far as northern Vietnam, about 250 kilometers away [scientificamerican.com#1][theconversation.com#1][scmp.com#1].

Protein analysis: Ancient proteins survived in all five sampled teeth. Four teeth showed an ameloblastin variant associated with Chinese Homo erectus fossils but lacked a second variant found in older specimens [sci.news#1][scientificamerican.com#1].
Cave deposits: Researchers recovered more than 18,000 mammal fossils from the caves and say porcupines likely accumulated many of the remains while collecting bones [livescience.com#1][enca.com#1].

perspectives.text: Paleoanthropologist Chris Stringer of the Natural History Museum in London said the late Chinese finds bring Homo erectus closer in age to late Javan examples and raise the possibility that populations connected during periods of lower sea levels [livescience.com#1].

Anthropologist John Hawks of the University of Wisconsin-Madison said the combined evidence from tooth shape and proteins makes a convincing case for late-surviving Homo erectus, but argued that researchers should compare the mystery tooth with more Denisovan teeth [livescience.com#1].

title: Webb traces Andromeda star merger, challenging common-envelope models
summary:
Astronomers say a smaller star spiraled into a red giant and merged with it in the Andromeda galaxy, marking the first closely tracked observation of this stage of binary-star evolution. The system, named AT 2025abao, brightened over several years before erupting in October 2025. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope observed it 47 days after the outburst peaked, helping researchers reconstruct the event [nasa.gov#1][sci.news#1][abc.net.au#1][sciencenews.org#1].

The team estimates that the giant had seven times the Sun’s mass and the companion about 0.7 times the Sun’s mass. Their interaction ended after about seven orbits, or seven years. The findings, published in Nature on Nov. 18, indicate that energy transport during the shared-envelope phase may be more complex than standard models describe. Researchers say continued observations are needed to determine the remnant’s state and confirm the merger [phys.org#1][sciencenews.org#1][newscientist.com#1][space.com#1].
quote: This is probably the most uncertain and critical phase in the evolution of a star
quote_author: Jason Nordhaus
talking_points: Ejected material: The eruption expelled an estimated 0.1 to 0.2 solar masses of material, while analysis suggests only about a tenth of the giant’s outer gas escaped [sci.news#1][sciencenews.org#1].
Early evolution: The giant swelled to more than twice its original size while its surface temperature barely changed [sciencenews.org#1].

More candidates: One research team has identified about 30 possible similar mergers, while the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope are expected to search for more [lineadirectaportal.com#1][abc.net.au#1].

perspectives.text: Jason Nordhaus of the Rochester Institute of Technology said nearly one-third of stars may go through the common-envelope phase. That share could be higher if engulfments of planets and other nonstellar objects are included, he said [newscientist.com#1].

technical_details: Common-envelope inspiral: As the smaller star moved through the giant’s shared gas envelope, drag removed orbital energy and drove it inward. Observations of this phase can help determine how binary systems lose orbital energy [nasa.gov#1][phys.org#1].

Infrared reconstruction: Webb’s mid-infrared measurements traced dust shed by the giant over centuries. Researchers matched the measurements to updated simulations to estimate the stars’ pre-eruption properties [nasa.gov#1][phys.org#1].
scientific_significance: Stellar energy transport: The observed evolution suggests energy from the inspiraling companion was redistributed through convection inside the expanded giant, rather than immediately inflating its atmosphere as some earlier models assumed [newscientist.com#1].

Evidence and uncertainty: Webb’s data and observations across ultraviolet, visible and infrared wavelengths support the merger reconstruction, but dust still obscures the remnant and researchers say follow-up observations are needed to settle its final state [nasa.gov#1][space.com#1][sciencenews.org#1].

Relevance to compact binaries: Common-envelope evolution is thought to help produce tightly bound pairs that can later become neutron stars or black holes; observing a system during the process supplies data for testing those pathways [nasa.gov#1][phys.org#1].

title: US loses measles elimination status as cases exceed 5,400
summary:
The United States lost its measles-elimination status on Nov. 17 after international health officials concluded the virus had spread continuously for at least 12 months, ending a designation the country had held since 2000 [arabtimesonline.com#1][elpais.com#1][arstechnica.com#1]. Pennsylvania reported another measles death the following day, bringing the state’s 2026 toll to eight [aljazeera.com#1].

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had counted 5,412 U.S. cases through Nov. 12, the highest annual total since 1991; Pennsylvania accounted for 1,589 cases [aljazeera.com#1][wisconsinexaminer.com#1][arstechnica.com#1]. Measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccination coverage among U.S. kindergarteners was 92.4% in the 2025-26 school year, below the roughly 95% level experts say is needed to prevent outbreaks [firstpost.com#1][elpais.com#1].

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional agency for the Americas, also revoked elimination status for Mexico and Bolivia [arabtimesonline.com#1][gbcghanaonline.com#1]. The three countries are expected to submit plans in the coming weeks to stop transmission. To regain elimination status, they must demonstrate that sustained spread has been interrupted for at least a year [arabtimesonline.com#1][gbcghanaonline.com#1].
quote: Measles elimination is not a trophy that is won once and placed on a shelf. It is an achievement that must be safeguarded every day by closing immunity gaps and ensuring we reach every community.
quote_author: Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, director of the Pan American Health Organization
talking_points: Review period: PAHO’s review relied on evidence from January 2025 through January 2026; the large Pennsylvania outbreak that began in April 2026 did not factor into the status decision [arstechnica.com#1].

Transmission evidence: Brewer cited measles cases reported every week since Jan. 20, 2025, and cases with no confirmed travel or contact source as evidence of sustained spread [arstechnica.com#1][wired.com#1].

Pregnancy risks: A federal public-health alert recorded 112 measles infections among pregnant women and 13 congenital cases in newborns from Jan. 1, 2025, through Sept. 28, 2026 [wisconsinexaminer.com#1].

Reported outcomes: Among the pregnant women whose outcomes were reported, two lost pregnancies. Eight of 19 live births were preterm, and eight newborns required neonatal intensive care [wisconsinexaminer.com#1].

State response: Pennsylvania said roughly 300 health-department staff were working with communities and providers and that the state had administered more than 11,500 MMR doses in 2026 [aljazeera.com#1].

perspectives.text: Pan American Health Organization: Director Jarbas Barbosa said the response should address barriers to care, missed vaccinations, misinformation and vaccine hesitancy, with broad vaccination campaigns, expanded laboratory testing and rapid case response [wired.com#1].

U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Director Erica Schwartz said losing the designation does not change the agency’s approach and that vaccination, rather than the status itself, protects people [wisconsinexaminer.com#1].

U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: Kennedy attributed vaccination gaps partly to COVID-era disruptions and said he continues to recommend MMR vaccination, while critics have faulted his previous public questioning of vaccine safety [wisconsinexaminer.com#1][firstpost.com#1].

WIRED reported that regaining elimination status could take years. William Moss said future efforts would require a stronger centralized federal response paired with very local work to identify under-vaccinated communities [wired.com#1].

Josh Michaud, KFF global and public-health policy expert: Michaud said the current administration has not communicated the need for vaccination with the urgency he saw from earlier administrations responding to measles outbreaks [firstpost.com#1].

suggested_qna.answer: Experts say the effort would require broad vaccination campaigns, expanded laboratory testing, rapid case response and contact tracing, alongside work to address barriers to care and vaccine hesitancy [wired.com#1].

historical_background: Before vaccination, nearly all U.S. children contracted measles by age 15; the disease caused an estimated 3 million to 4 million infections, 48,000 hospitalizations and 400 to 500 deaths annually [sciencebasedmedicine.org#1]. title: Chad study finds eagles may prey on 26-kilogram baboons
summary:
Researchers have found marks on bones and skulls suggesting Verreaux’s eagles preyed on adult male olive baboons in Chad’s Ennedi Plateau, including one estimated to have weighed 26.2 kilograms. The study, published Nov. 18 in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology, challenges a longstanding rule of thumb that primates above about 13 kilograms were effectively beyond avian predation. Previously, no primate heavier than that had been confirmed killed by a raptor [wiley.com#1][popsci.com#1][livescience.com#1].

The team documented punctured eye sockets and talon-like scrapes on shoulder blades among the baboon remains. It did not witness a kill, so the researchers describe eagle predation as a likely explanation rather than a directly observed event [wiley.com#1][discovermagazine.com#1]. Some early hominins were in a similar weight range, but the findings do not establish that eagles hunted adult hominins or influenced their defensive behavior. The researchers plan further study of the isolated baboon population and its behavior [popsci.com#1][gizmodo.com#1].
quote: At first, the idea of eagles hunting adult male baboons seemed to exist on the thin edge of possibility, until it didn’t. Our skepticism slowly gave way to acceptance. The evidence was convincing.
quote_author: Nathaniel Dominy, senior author and an anthropologist and evolutionary biologist at Dartmouth College
talking_points: Sample details: The initial sample contained nine baboons, including eight adult males; researchers estimated a mean body mass of 22.2 kilograms [wiley.com#1][gizmodo.com#1].
Bone evidence: Two males had punctured eye sockets, and researchers identified a scapula with scrapes in a pattern associated with eagle feeding [wiley.com#1][discovermagazine.com#1].

Possible defense: Researchers observed baboons sounding alarm calls and moving to safety when Verreaux’s eagles flew overhead; primates may also mob aerial predators by charging them [discovermagazine.com#1][gizmodo.com#1].

perspectives.text: Robert Simmons, a researcher at the FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology, called the finding rare and said limited prey in the dry desert could lead Verreaux’s eagles to hunt larger, riskier animals [livescience.com#1].

W. Scott McGraw, an anthropology professor at Ohio State University, said early hominins, particularly infants and juveniles, may have been vulnerable to raptors and could have relied on group living, warning calls and safer habitats [livescience.com#1].
